Given, $\sqrt{1+\sin ^{2} \alpha}=\sqrt{5} \sqrt{1-\sin ^{2} \alpha}$

$\begin{array}{l}$

\Rightarrow $\alpha=\sin ^{-1} \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}=\tan ^{-1} \sqrt{2}$

questions.q: The eccentricity of a rectangular hyperbola is
questions.solution:
The general equation of a hyperbola is \$(\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=$1\), where \(a\) represents the transverse of hyperbola and \(b\) represents the conjugate of the hyperbola.
The eccentricity of a hyperbola is \$(e=\frac{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}{a} \cdots($1)\).
Since a rectangular hyperbola is defined as a hyperbola whose transverse axis is identical to its conjugate axis, \(a=b\).
Substitute \(a=b\) into (1).
\(\begin{aligned}
& $e=\frac{\sqrt{a^2+b^2}}{a}$\\
& \Rightarrow $e=\frac{\sqrt{a^2+a^2}}{a}$\\
& \Rightarrow $e=\frac{\sqrt{2 a^2}}{a}$\\
& \Rightarrow $e=\frac{\sqrt{2} a}{a}$\\
& \Rightarrow $e=\sqrt{2}$
\end{aligned}\)

questions.q: The distance between the foci of the hyperbola $x^2-3 y^2-4 x-6 y-11=0$ is
questions.solution:
Given, equation of hyperbola is $\begin{gathered}$x²-3 y²-4 x-6 y-11=0 \\
\Rightarrow \quad\left($x^2-4 x+4\right)-3\left($y^2+2 y+1\right)-11 \\
=4-3 \\
\Rightarrow \quad(x-2)^2-3(y+1)^2=12 \\
\Rightarrow \quad $\frac{(x-2)^2}{12}-\frac{(y+1)^2}{4}=$1 \\
$\text { Now, } \quad$e=$\sqrt{1+\frac{4}{12}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}
\end{gathered}$Now, e=$\sqrt{1+\frac{4}{12}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\therefore$ Distance between foci =2 a e=2 $\times \sqrt{12} \times \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}=$8

questions.q: A hyperbola passing through a focus of the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{169}+\frac{y^2}{25}=1$. Its transverse and conjugate axes coincide respectively with the major and minor axes of the ellipse. The product of eccentricities is 1 . Then, the equation of the hyperbola is
questions.solution:
Let the equation of hyperbola be $\frac{x^2}{a^2}-\frac{y^2}{b^2}=$1 Given equation of ellipse is $\frac{x^2}{(13)^2}+\frac{y^2}{(5)^2}=$1 Here, $\begin{aligned}$& $\text { Here, } \quad$a=13, b=5 \\
& \therefore \quad e=$\sqrt{1-\frac{b^2}{a^2}}$\\
& \therefore \quad=$\sqrt{1-\frac{25}{169}}=\sqrt{\frac{144}{169}}=\frac{12}{13}$\\
& \therefore $\text { Focus }( \pm$a e, 0)=\left( \pm$13 $\times \frac{12}{13},$0\right) \\
& \quad=( $\pm$12,0)
\end{aligned} Since, Eq. (i) passes through $( \pm 12,0)$. $\begin{array}{rrrl}
\therefore$& $\frac{144}{a^2}-\frac{0}{b^2}=$1 \\
\Rightarrow & a²=144 \\
\Rightarrow & a= $\pm$12
\end{array} Now eccentricity of hyperbola $\begin{aligned}$e^{\prime} & =$\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{a^2}}$\\
& =$\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{144}}
\end{aligned}$According to the equation, $\begin{array}{rlrl}$& e^{\prime}=1 \\
\Rightarrow & & $\frac{12}{13} \times \sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{144}}$& =1 \\
\Rightarrow & & $\sqrt{1+\frac{b^2}{144}}$& =$\frac{13}{12}$\\
\Rightarrow & & 1+$\frac{b^2}{144}$& =$\frac{169}{144}$\\
\Rightarrow & & $\frac{b^2}{144}$& =$\frac{169}{144}-$1 \\
\Rightarrow & & $\frac{b^2}{144}$& =$\frac{25}{144}$\\
b² & =25
\end{array} $\therefore$ Equation of hyperbola is $\frac{x^2}{144}-\frac{y^2}{25}=$1
$

questions.q: The equation \left|\sqrt{x^{2} + {\left(y - 1\right)}^{2}} - \sqrt{x^{2} + {\left(y + 1\right)}^{2}}\right| = K$ will represent a hyperbola for -$
questions.solution:
We have \left|\sqrt{x^{2} + {\left(y - 1\right)}^{2}} - \sqrt{x^{2} + {\left(y + 1\right)}^{2}}\right| = K$

Which is equivalent to \left|{S}_{1}P - {S}_{2}P\right|= Const .$

Where ${S}_{1} ≡ \left(0, 1\right), {S}_{2} ≡ \left($0, -1\right)$ .and $P ≡ \left(x, y\right)$

Using properties of a hyperbola, the above equation represents a hyperbola, then we have.

$2a = K$ [where $2a$ is the transverse axis and e is the eccentricity]

and $2ae = {S}_{1}{S}_{2} = 2$

Dividing, we have $e = \dfrac{2}{K}$

Since, $e > 1$ for a hyperbola, therefore $K < 2$

Also, $K$ must be a positive quantity. Hence, we have, $K \in \left(0, 2\right)$ .$

questions.solution: Given hyperbola $\begin{aligned} x^2-y^2-4 x+2 y+c & =0 \\ (x-2)^2-(y-1)^2 & =3-c \\ \frac{(x-2)^2}{3-c}-\frac{(y-1)^2}{3-c} & =1 \end{aligned}$ Focus of hyperbola is $\begin{aligned} x-2 & = \pm \sqrt{(3-c)+(3-c)} \\ x-2 & = \pm \sqrt{6-2 c} \quad[\because a e=\sqrt{(3-c)+(3-c)}] \\ x & =2 \pm \sqrt{6-2 c} \end{aligned}$ Here, $2+\sqrt{6-2 c}=2+2 \sqrt{2}\therefore \quad \sqrt{6-2 c}=2 \sqrt{2} \Rightarrow 6-2 c=8 \Rightarrow c=-1$

questions.solution: Equation of ellipse $\frac{x^2}{16}+\frac{y^2}{25}=1$ Foci $\quad=(0, \pm 3)\Rightarrow \quad e_2=\sqrt{1-\frac{16}{25}}=\frac{3}{5}$ given $e_2 e_2=1$ (where $e_2$ is eccentricity of hyperbola) Let equation of hyperbola $-\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1$ its passes through $(0, \pm 3)\begin{array}{ll} \therefore$& b²=9 \\ \Rightarrow & e_2=$\sqrt{1+\frac{a^2}{b^2}}$\\ \Rightarrow & e_2^2=1+$\frac{a^2}{b^2}$\\ \Rightarrow & $\frac{1}{e_2^2}=$1+$\frac{a^2}{9} \Rightarrow \frac{25}{9}=$1+$\frac{a^2}{9}$\\ \Rightarrow & a²=16 \end{array} Hence, the equation of hyperbola is $\frac{y^2}{9}-\frac{x^2}{16}=1$

Distance between foci& $= 8 = 2ae$

questions.q: If two points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the hyperbola $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1 ( a < b )$, whose centre $C$ be such that $CP$ is perpendicular to $CQ$, then the value of $\dfrac{1}{CP^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{CQ^{2}}$ is
questions.solution:
Let $CP = {r}_{1}$ be inclined to transverse axis at an angle $\theta$ such that $P \left({r}_{1}$cos ⁡ $\theta, {r}_{1}$sin ⁡ $\theta\right) lies on the hyperbola. Therefore,

${r}_{1}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta}{b^{2}}\right) =$1$

Replacing $\thetaby{90}^{o} + $\theta, we get,

${r}_{2}^{2}\left(\dfrac{\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta}{b^{2}}\right) =$1$

(where, $CQ = {r}_{2}$)

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{{r}_{1}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{r}_{2}^{2}} = \dfrac{\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta}{b^{2}} + \dfrac{\sin^{2} ⁡ \theta}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{\cos^{2} ⁡ \theta}{b^{2}}

$⇒ 1{r}_{1}^{2} + 1{r}_{2}^{2} = \cos^{2} ⁡ $\theta \left(\dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{b2}\right) + \sin^{2}$⁡ $\theta\left(\dfrac{1}{a2} - \dfrac{1}{b2}\right)

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{{r}_{1}^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{r}_{2}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{b^{2}}

$⇒ $\dfrac{1}{CP^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{CQ^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{a^{2}} - \dfrac{1}{b^{2}}

$

questions.q: If a directrix of a hyperbola centered at the origin and passing through the point  \left(4, - 2\sqrt{3}\right)$ is $5x = 4\sqrt{5}$~and~its eccentricity is $e$, then:$
questions.solution:
Let equation of hyperbola is $\dfrac{x2}{a2} - \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$

$∴$ It passes through \left(4, - 2\sqrt{3}\right) ⇒ \dfrac{16}{a2} - \dfrac{12}{b2} = 1$

$⇒ 16 - 12 \times \dfrac{a2}{b2} = a^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

Equation of directrix is $x = $\dfrac{a}{e} = \dfrac{4}{5},given in question.

$⇒ a^{2} = $\dfrac{16}{5}$e^{2} . . . \left(2\right)$

And we know that $b^{2} = a^{2} \left(e^{2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ $\dfrac{b2}{a2} =$e^{2} - 1 . . . \left($3\right)$

$∴$ From~ \left($1\right), \left($2\right) \text{ and } \left(3\right)$

$16 - $\dfrac{12}{e^{2} - 1} = \dfrac{16}{5}$e^{2}$

$⇒ 16e^{2} - 16 - 12 = $\dfrac{16e^{2}}{5} \left(e^{2} - 1\right)$

$⇒ 4e^{4} - 24e^{2} + 35 = 0$
